path.description: Marlin 4-bit GEMM forward. When a column slice is split across several thread blocks (slice_count > 1), each block adds its fp32 fragment to the fp16 partial already in the output C, in slice order, under a per-column lock. No atomic add is used; the read-modify-write on C is an ordinary load, add and store executed by one block at a time.

evidence.claim: barrier_acquire(&locks[slice_col], slice_idx) spins until the lock equals this block's slice index, so slices enter in order 0, 1, 2, ...
barrier_acquire: ld.global.acquire.gpu.b32 loop until state == count
frag_c[...] += __half2float(c_red[j]): fp32 register accumulate of the fp16 partial read from C; then C[...] = __float2half(...) unless last
barrier_release(&locks[slice_col], last) increments the lock (red.relaxed.gpu.global.add.s32) or resets it on the last slice
slice_idx and slice_count are derived from the static striped partitioning of k_tiles, not from runtime arrival

notes: Serialised split-K reduce: the order is fixed by slice_idx, which is a function of the block's static tile assignment. Partials are rounded to fp16 between slices (a precision choice, not a determinism issue). This is the pattern Cankaya 2026 observed as deterministic for GPTQ with Marlin enabled.

path.description: Lock word increment that releases the next slice in the serialised global reduce.

evidence.claim: called once per slice by the block that holds the lock, so at most one increment is in flight

notes: Integer lock counter; exact. It orders the float reduce (that is its purpose) but the order it imposes is the static slice order, so the downstream reduction order cannot change. Not B-indirect.
